expressions.register: Use it when identifying the limiting part that must be understood before adding more resources elsewhere.
expressions.misuse: Do not call the busiest component a bottleneck without evidence that it constrains overall performance.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: Report latency is measured from the client's request until the completed report response arrives.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when explaining response speed, specifying the measurement boundary and any relevant percentile.
expressions.misuse: Do not quote average latency as if it describes the slowest customers or compare measurements with different start points.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: Job submission is idempotent when retrying the same request identifier does not create an additional job.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when discussing retries, duplicate delivery, or operations that may be repeated after an uncertain response.
expressions.misuse: Do not equate idempotent with identical responses or no side effects; the intended state-changing effect is what matters.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: The rollback restores the previous export implementation while retaining the incident logs for investigation.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when comparing recovery options and explaining how a problematic deployment can be reversed.
expressions.misuse: Do not assume a code rollback reverses database migrations or customer-visible side effects; verify the recovery boundary.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: Psychological safety lets an engineer admit they do not understand a migration before approving it under pressure.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when discussing whether engineering conversations make uncertainty and concerns visible early enough to act on them.
expressions.misuse: Do not equate psychological safety with avoiding disagreement or lowering technical standards; respectful challenge remains essential.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: My developmental feedback is to request a database reviewer when a change alters persistence guarantees you cannot yet assess.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when a review should build engineering judgement as well as improve the current patch.
expressions.misuse: Do not use you are careless as developmental feedback; explain the observed decision, its consequence, and a better next action.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: Our hypothesis is that export failures occur when the new timeout expires before the final database read.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it during debugging when an explanation guides investigation but has not yet been established.
expressions.misuse: Do not promote a plausible hypothesis to root cause merely because it fits the first few logs.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: Report throughput has plateaued at four hundred completed jobs per minute despite the extra workers.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when discussing processing capacity or completed work rather than the delay experienced by one request.
expressions.misuse: Do not confuse incoming request rate with completed throughput or compare tests using substantially different workloads.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: Our measured service level tracks successful valid job submissions rather than only whether the server responds to health checks.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when discussing service performance from a clearly defined consumer perspective.
expressions.misuse: Do not assume service level automatically means a contractual guarantee; distinguish measurement, target, and any agreement.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: We should triage the sign-in failures before investigating the lower-impact dashboard warning.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when several signals or issues compete for attention and an initial response order is needed.
expressions.misuse: Do not use triage to mean a complete diagnosis; its purpose is initial assessment and routing.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: The escalation asks the identity owner to assess token rejection; it does not assume that their service caused it.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when incident recovery needs permissions, knowledge, or decisions beyond the current response team.
expressions.misuse: Do not send an escalation with only urgent; include impact, evidence, actions already taken, and the specific help required.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: Disabling the new export path is mitigation because it reduces customer failures while diagnosis continues.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it during incident coordination to distinguish reducing harm from completing the underlying repair.
expressions.misuse: Do not announce resolution solely because a mitigation is active; verify customer recovery and track the remaining defect.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: Malformed partner files remain a residual risk because validation can stop unsafe processing but cannot guarantee timely replacement data.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when reviewers need to understand what safeguards do not eliminate before approving a design or release.
expressions.misuse: Do not claim risk is resolved simply because validation was implemented; describe the remaining failure and its practical consequence.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: The migration path includes field mapping, sample requests, test credentials, and checks for changed shipping-status meanings.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when technical consumers must make specific adaptations to adopt a replacement safely.
expressions.misuse: Do not call a new endpoint URL a complete migration path if authentication, field semantics, or error handling also changes.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: Keeping the old notification path temporarily improves reversibility while the team evaluates the shared event bus.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when deciding how much evidence or caution a commitment needs before adoption.
expressions.misuse: Do not assume code reversibility means data or operational consequences are also reversible; examine each separately.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: Two application instances provide redundancy only if the surviving instance can serve the required traffic.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when discussing duplicate resources and how they support continuity under a defined failure.
expressions.misuse: Do not assume duplication removes risk if both copies depend on the same power source, credentials, or configuration.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: We raised the severity after confirming that sign-in failures affect all newly registered customers.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when coordinating the response level and communicating how serious the verified impact is.
expressions.misuse: Do not assume severity labels mean the same thing across organisations or confuse severity with a developer's workload priority.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: The impact assessment compares failed sign-ins by region and checks whether existing sessions can still submit work.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when technical signals need to be translated into consequences for users or dependent services.
expressions.misuse: Do not equate the number of alerts with the amount of customer impact; investigate affected journeys and populations.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: A shared token configuration has a larger potential blast radius than a change isolated to one regional instance.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it in risk and incident discussions to explain how far a problem may spread or be contained.
expressions.misuse: Do not describe the potential blast radius as confirmed impact; distinguish architectural exposure from observed failures.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: We can reproduce the export failure with the archived test dataset and the current timeout configuration.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when a repeatable observation is needed to investigate a defect or verify a proposed correction.
expressions.misuse: Do not claim a failure is fixed simply because you cannot reproduce it on a different dataset or environment.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: We will isolate the timeout change by keeping the dataset and all other export settings unchanged.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when multiple possible causes need to be examined independently during testing or diagnosis.
expressions.misuse: Do not describe a test as isolating one variable if traffic, data, and configuration all change together.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: Exporting one month at a time is a workaround while the team investigates failures in larger datasets.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when customers or support need a practical temporary route to complete affected work.
expressions.misuse: Do not describe a workaround as a fix or recommend it without checking whether it preserves data completeness.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: The interface contract promises a currency code with every amount, not just a numeric total.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it in design and review discussions when consumers need stable, testable expectations across a component boundary.
expressions.misuse: Do not reduce the contract to a schema alone if ordering, failure behaviour, or meaning is also promised.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: Keeping the existing amount field during the transition preserves backward compatibility for mobile clients that have not updated.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when evaluating whether a change can be introduced without requiring existing consumers to change immediately.
expressions.misuse: Do not assume an added field is always compatible; strict parsers or changed semantics may still break consumers.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: Capacity planning includes the database connections needed during the sale, not only application server count.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when forecasts must become resource decisions before a launch, migration, or demand peak.
expressions.misuse: Do not plan only for average traffic or assume every request consumes the same amount of resources.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: The sale's load profile includes short payment bursts and larger baskets, unlike ordinary browsing traffic.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when explaining why a performance test must resemble the work the production system will actually perform.
expressions.misuse: Do not describe a load profile using request count alone if expensive operations or burst patterns drive the risk.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: The shared configuration store is a single point of failure if every checkout request requires it to respond.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when identifying a dependency that can defeat otherwise redundant parts of an architecture.
collocations: remove a single point of failure
identify a single point of failure
expressions.misuse: Do not label every unique component a single point of failure without explaining what stops when it fails.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: Duplicated invoice rules create technical debt because each price change requires coordinated edits in three handlers.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when explaining a concrete future cost that justifies improving an existing technical approach.
expressions.misuse: Do not use technical debt as a label for every old technology or any code you personally dislike.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: One tested invoice calculation improves maintainability because future rule changes no longer require three separate edits.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when evaluating how a design affects ongoing engineering effort and the safety of future changes.
expressions.misuse: Do not equate maintainability with fewer lines of code; compressed or highly abstract code may be harder to change.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: Our observability gap is the missing link between failed requests and the database operation that delayed them.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when explaining whether engineers can answer useful questions about production behaviour from available signals.
expressions.misuse: Do not equate observability with collecting more logs indiscriminately; useful context and connections matter more than volume alone.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: The telemetry records request duration, deployment version, and the database operation name without including customer payloads.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when discussing the operational signals needed to investigate or monitor a service.
expressions.misuse: Do not collect sensitive request contents merely because more telemetry might be useful; choose purposeful fields and safeguards.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: There is a correlation between peak traffic and failures, but the deployment happened during the same period.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when describing a pattern honestly while keeping the causal explanation open to investigation.
expressions.misuse: Do not use correlation proves the cause; simultaneous changes and other factors can explain the observed relationship.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: The large-account result is inconclusive because the prototype test included only accounts with a few hundred records.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when results do not yet justify either accepting or rejecting a particular technical claim.
expressions.misuse: Do not use inconclusive to mean the idea has failed or to avoid naming the evidence that is missing.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: Our working assumption is that account size changes cache behaviour enough to require a separate benchmark.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when engineering must proceed before every uncertainty is resolved, while making the basis of planning visible.
expressions.misuse: Do not let a working assumption silently become a permanent architecture requirement without reviewing the evidence.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: The retry policy permits three attempts for transient connection failures but does not repeat invalid job requests.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when specifying recovery behaviour rather than assuming a library's default retries fit every operation.
expressions.misuse: Do not retry every failure indefinitely or layer independent retries without considering their combined load and delay.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: Exponential backoff increases the wait between failed submissions, while jitter helps avoid clients retrying together.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when explaining how a retry mechanism reduces repeated pressure during a transient service problem.
expressions.misuse: Do not imply backoff guarantees recovery or removes the need for attempt limits and safe operation semantics.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: The activity counter uses eventual consistency, so a recently added event may not appear immediately in every region.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when explaining the consistency guarantee and user-visible behaviour of asynchronously replicated data.
expressions.misuse: Do not imply eventual consistency alone promises a fixed convergence time or is suitable for every financial decision.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: A stale read shows the previous activity count because the regional replica has not applied the latest update.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when distinguishing data freshness from a missing write, permanent data loss, or an interface rendering issue.
expressions.misuse: Do not assume every old-looking value proves replication lag; caching or the write path may be responsible.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: A race condition lets two workers read the same count and overwrite each other's increment with the same new value.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when investigating correctness problems caused by concurrent operations interacting without adequate coordination.
expressions.misuse: Do not label every intermittent failure a race condition; identify the competing operations and the harmful ordering.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: The service-level objective targets successful completion of eligible submissions over a rolling twenty-eight-day window.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when teams need an explicit reliability target that can inform engineering and product decisions.
expressions.misuse: Do not give a percentage without defining the events, exclusions, and window or confuse an objective with a contractual agreement.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: The failed submissions consumed much of the error budget, triggering our policy to prioritise reliability work before further expansion.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when connecting reliability performance to agreed choices about release risk and improvement work.
expressions.misuse: Do not describe an error budget as permission to cause avoidable failures or quote remaining budget without its measurement basis.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: The queue invariant is that every accepted job remains recoverable until its completion is durably recorded.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.
expressions.register: Use it when code review needs to identify a correctness condition that must survive normal and failure paths.
expressions.misuse: Do not label a common observation an invariant unless the design genuinely requires it to hold in the specified scope.

expressions.title: A familiar role situation
expressions.plain: Use your own words to communicate the intent.
expressions.precise: A durable completion record is a precondition for permanently removing the accepted job from the recovery queue.
expressions.diplomatic: Choose wording that respects the audience and the situation.

scenarios.prompt: An interviewer asks why you tested a small version before committing to a larger rollout. Explain your choice in two sentences.
scenarios.focus: Explain why you chose an approach
scenarios.exampleResponse: The rationale for testing a small version was to identify problems before committing more resources. We used the feedback to change the rollout plan.
scenarios.freshPrompt: A colleague asks why you gathered a second opinion before making a recommendation. Explain the choice and the benefit.
scenarios.freshExampleResponse: The rationale for seeking a second opinion was to challenge our assumptions. It helped us make a more balanced recommendation.

scenarios.prompt: In an interview, you describe checking a supplier's claimed time saving before recommending a trial. Explain what information you looked for and what you would still need to know.
scenarios.exampleResponse: I looked for records that could substantiate the claimed time saving. Before recommending a trial, I would check whether the comparison covered similar work and conditions.
scenarios.freshPrompt: An interviewer asks how you would evaluate a proposal based on a single positive report. Explain how you would test its reliability without dismissing the source.
scenarios.freshExampleResponse: I would seek information that could substantiate the report, including how it was collected and what it leaves out. I would compare it with a second source before committing.

scenarios.prompt: A teammate says a plan must work because they feel certain. You are unconvinced. Respond respectfully and ask for one concrete way to test the claim.
scenarios.exampleResponse: Confidence is useful, but what evidence would substantiate that claim? Could we agree on a small test before making the commitment?
scenarios.freshPrompt: Someone thinks an outside example settles a disagreement about your team's plan. Ask how to check whether that example applies to your situation, while acknowledging what it contributes.
scenarios.freshExampleResponse: That example is helpful context. To substantiate the claim for our team, could we compare the conditions and gather information from a small trial?

scenarios.prompt: During an interview, you are asked about a time you had to choose between speed and depth of checking. Describe the competing outcomes and explain your decision using fictional details.
scenarios.exampleResponse: The trade-off was delivery speed versus a more thorough check. I chose a smaller verified release, then planned the remaining work.
scenarios.freshPrompt: An interviewer asks how you would choose between a familiar process and a more tailored but slower option. Explain what you would consider before deciding.
scenarios.freshExampleResponse: I would make the trade-off between immediate consistency and extra tailoring explicit. Then I would check which needs are essential and test the simplest option that meets them.

scenarios.prompt: A colleague predicts a large improvement but has only one early observation. Ask a respectful question before the team commits.
scenarios.exampleResponse: Could we examine the evidence that would substantiate that estimate? One observation is a starting point, but we need to understand how representative it is.
scenarios.freshPrompt: A different team claims a new approach saves time. Ask what information would make that claim credible.
scenarios.freshExampleResponse: What records could substantiate the claim that the approach saves time? Could we compare similar work before and after the change?

scenarios.prompt: You can deliver a smaller change this week or a broader change later. Explain both sides and recommend a next step.
scenarios.exampleResponse: The trade-off is earlier value versus a broader solution. I recommend the smaller change first, with a review before adding more scope.
scenarios.freshPrompt: A team can use a standard solution quickly or customise it with more effort. Explain the choice without promising both advantages.
scenarios.freshExampleResponse: The trade-off is speed versus customisation. Let's identify which requirements truly need a custom approach before deciding.

scenarios.prompt: Two colleagues describe the same event differently. Invite them to compare their accounts without choosing a winner.
scenarios.exampleResponse: Could we reconcile the differences between these accounts before reaching a conclusion? Let's identify what each person observed and what remains unclear.
scenarios.freshPrompt: Two written summaries give different dates for the same milestone. Propose a calm next step.
scenarios.freshExampleResponse: Let's reconcile the records by checking the source of each date. We can then explain the difference and confirm the milestone together.

scenarios.prompt: A colleague says a change adds work and feels their concern was dismissed. Respond before defending the change.
scenarios.exampleResponse: I acknowledge your concern about the extra workload. Could we look at the tasks that have changed and what support would help?
scenarios.freshPrompt: Someone worries that a decision was made without hearing their view. Recognise the concern without claiming you agree with every point.
scenarios.freshExampleResponse: I acknowledge your concern about how the decision was made. Let's hear the perspective we missed and identify what can still be reconsidered.

scenarios.prompt: People ask for a final date that has not been confirmed. State the limit of what you know and offer a concrete update.
scenarios.focus: Be honest about what you do not know
scenarios.exampleResponse: There is uncertainty about the final date. We can confirm the next step today, and I will share the remaining timing information on Friday.
scenarios.freshPrompt: A colleague asks whether a planned change will affect their work. You do not yet know the full details. Answer honestly.
scenarios.freshExampleResponse: There is uncertainty about the impact on each role. I will share what we know now and arrange a further update when the remaining questions are answered.

scenarios.prompt: In a fictional healthcare communication interview, explain how you would respond to someone who is distressed without promising an outcome.
scenarios.exampleResponse: I would respond with empathy by listening to what worries the person most. I would check my understanding before explaining what support is available.
scenarios.freshPrompt: A fictional colleague asks how you would speak with someone who feels ignored. Describe your communication approach.
scenarios.freshExampleResponse: I would show empathy by asking what the experience has been like and listening without rushing to reassure. Then I would check which concern matters most to them.

scenarios.prompt: In a fictional handover, an important piece of information seems absent. Raise the issue and suggest checking it. Do not make a clinical recommendation.
scenarios.exampleResponse: My concern is that an important detail may be missing from the handover. Could we check the source together before completing it?
scenarios.freshPrompt: In a fictional team update, two summaries contain inconsistent details. Raise the possible issue without claiming you know which is wrong.
scenarios.freshExampleResponse: My concern is that the summaries may give different impressions. Could we compare the details and confirm the intended message?

scenarios.prompt: A shared action has no named owner. Ask who will answer for the outcome and when progress will be reviewed.
scenarios.exampleResponse: Who will be accountable for the outcome? Let's confirm the owner, available support and the date for our next progress review.
scenarios.freshPrompt: Several people contribute to an improvement, but nobody knows who should provide the final update. Clarify ownership without assigning blame.
scenarios.freshExampleResponse: Could we confirm who is accountable for the final outcome and who will provide the update? Each contributor should also know which part they own.

scenarios.prompt: The group wants to commit immediately, but you see a reason to test a smaller option first. Challenge the decision respectfully.
scenarios.exampleResponse: I want to offer constructive dissent: a smaller test could reveal problems before we commit. Could we compare that option against the immediate rollout?
scenarios.freshPrompt: A team repeats an approach that did not work last time. Invite a different option while respecting the shared aim.
scenarios.freshExampleResponse: Could we make space for constructive dissent about the approach? I support the aim, but a different sequence may address the problem we saw last time.

scenarios.prompt: In a fictional healthcare communication interview, explain how you would raise a concern when a more senior colleague interrupts you.
scenarios.exampleResponse: I would remain assertive by stating the concern clearly and respectfully. I would ask to finish the point, then invite the colleague's perspective.
scenarios.freshPrompt: In a fictional discussion, someone repeatedly talks over a colleague. Explain a respectful way to protect their opportunity to speak.
scenarios.freshExampleResponse: An assertive response could be: let's hear the end of their point before responding. That protects the discussion without attacking anyone.

scenarios.prompt: A colleague's update lacks the context needed to understand its recommendation. Offer one useful improvement.
scenarios.focus: Give feedback someone can act on
scenarios.exampleResponse: My constructive feedback is to add the missing context before the recommendation. That would help the reader understand why the next step makes sense.
scenarios.freshPrompt: A colleague's summary contains useful detail but its next step is unclear. Give specific feedback with a reason.
scenarios.freshExampleResponse: A constructive suggestion is to finish with one explicit next step. That would help the reader know what action is being requested.
